ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Using a freshly prepared potato suspension containing catalase to carry out an experiment of decomposing H2O2, the results of two groups of experiments are shown in the figure. The curve of group 1 is the result of adding 0.5 mL enzyme suspension to 5 mL 1% H2O2 solution under the conditions of pH=7.0 and 20℃. Compared with group 1, group 2 made only one change in the experiment. What did group 2 increase? (Choose one from the concentration of enzyme in the suspension, the concentration of H2O2 solution, the temperature of the reaction system, and the pH of the reaction system)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Using a freshly prepared potato suspension containing catalase to carry out an experiment of decomposing H2O2, the results of two groups of experiments are shown in the figure. The curve of group 1 is the result of adding 0.5 mL enzyme suspension to 5 mL 1% H2O2 solution under the conditions of pH=7.0 and 20℃. Compared with group 1, group 2 made only one change in the experiment. What did group 2 increase? (Choose one from the concentration of enzyme in the suspension, the concentration of H2O2 solution, the temperature of the reaction system, and the pH of the reaction system)
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the horizontal axis is reaction time, and the vertical axis is the relative value of the total amount of O2 produced. The curve of group 1 is represented by hollow diamonds; it rises with time and then reaches a plateau at about 0.9–1.0. The curve of group 2 is represented by solid squares; it rises faster and reaches a plateau at about 1.9, and the final total amount of O2 produced is clearly about twice that of group 1. Then reason: The stem states that the conditions of group 1 are pH=7.0, 20℃, 5 mL 1% H2O2 solution plus 0.5 mL enzyme suspension, and group 2 changed only one factor. If the enzyme concentration is increased, it will mainly accelerate the reaction rate, but with the substrate amount unchanged, the final total amount of O2 generally does not change; if temperature or pH is changed, it also mainly affects enzyme activity and reaction rate, and cannot make the total amount of O2 after complete decomposition of the substrate increase to about twice. In the figure, the final plateau value of group 2 is clearly higher, indicating that the total amount of decomposable H2O2 increased, so the change was increasing the concentration of the H2O2 solution.
